To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the use of the 5-item HADS is a valid measure of psychological distress in head and neck cancer patients, 2) the 5-item scale has high internal consistency and test-retest reliability, 3) the scale correlates with other measures of psychological distress, 4) the scale has a good ability to discriminate between distressed and non-distressed patients, and 5) the 5-items are the best items from the original 14-item HADS scale.
